sources.title: ISODISTORT: Displacement mode, normalization and parent phase/distortion phase
ISOTROPY: order parameter Direction and Invariants
SpinW: Commutative Hamiltonian and linear spin waves
Phonopy: quasiharmonic approximation , thermal expansion and constant pressure heat capacity
Phonopy: Harmonic vibration free energy and thermodynamic formula

modules.title: Structural distortion decomposition and mode coupling
modules.summary: Extract displacements from aligned structure pairs, project onto mode bases, then study competition and coexistence of two order parameters.

modules.title: magnetic exchange , magnons and spin waves
modules.summary: Connect exchange parameters, precession modes, and excitation dispersions in ferromagnetic and two-sublattice antiferromagnetic chains.

modules.title: Quasiharmonic approximation and thermal expansion
modules.summary: From multi-volume static energy and vibration free energy, find the finite temperature equilibrium volume, thermal expansion and constant pressure heat capacity.

lessons.title: Align the unit cells first, then talk about distortion
lessons.summary: Origin, periodic images, and strains can all be disguised as atomic displacements.

sections.title: Structure pairs must have a common reference
sections.text: The parent phase and the distorted phase must first be converted to the same compatible unit cell base, with the same number of elements and atoms. The first version of this site requires users to confirm this correspondence and not automatically interpret any two structures as before and after a phase change.

sections.title: Atomic correspondence does not only compare list indexes
sections.text: Automatic matching is subject to element identity and global one-to-one relationships. When atoms of the same type have equivalent distances or multiple feasible matches, the atomic mapping should be provided explicitly; otherwise, the pattern amplitude has no unique meaning.

sections.title: The shortest periodic displacement of a non-orthogonal unit cell
sections.text: Fractional-coordinate differences can include integer lattice vectors. Choose the nearest periodic image by Cartesian distance; independently wrapping components into half intervals need not find the shortest distance in a skew cell.

sections.title: Separate uniform strain from internal displacement
sections.text: Use the parent lattice Lp as the reference metric, with u_ref=Δf Lp. The lattice deformation gradient F=(Lp⁻¹Ld)ᵀ gives homogeneous strain E=(FᵀF−I)/2; internal displacements in the actual distorted cell are u_ref Fᵀ. Mode projection uses the parent reference frame. Overall translation may be removed using the arithmetic mean over atoms rather than a mass-weighted center of mass.

lessons.title: Reconstruct atomic distortions from mode coordinates
lessons.summary: A mode amplitude is meaningful only if it is saved together with the base and normalization.

sections.title: Modes are directions in displacement space
sections.text: Stack the three-dimensional displacements of N atoms into a 3N-dimensional vector. Currently using Cartesian geometric displacements, the mode is normalized by the Euclidean norm and should not be confused with mass weighting phonon eigenvectors.

sections.title: Orthogonal and non-orthogonal bases
sections.text: For orthonormal modes, amplitudes are Bᵀu. For nonorthogonal independent modes, solve least squares; separate dot products double-count contributions. A rank-deficient basis gives no unique amplitudes.

sections.title: What is missing from the residual answer?
sections.text: Reconstruction includes only the supplied mode space. A large residual means these modes do not fully describe the structural displacement; it does not automatically identify another irrep.

sections.title: From linear patterns to exportable structures
sections.text: Drag the amplitude to reconstruct the structure and export it. The SrTiO₃ example uses the small-displacement oxygen rotation mode in compatible supercell ; the linear displacement is not a rigid octahedral rotation at any finite angle. The mode name is the site description tag.

lessons.title: How do two order parameter compete and coexist?
lessons.summary: First check that the free energy is bounded, then find all stationary points and compare the energies.

sections.title: A verifiable bimodal model
sections.text: Use an even teaching free energy invariant under independently reversing each order parameter. Actual material terms require specific representations and momentum conservation; this formula does not automatically describe arbitrary pairs of distortions.

sections.title: Higher-order terms determine whether energy has a lower bound
sections.text: b1,b2>0 and c>−2√(b1b2) guarantee a strictly stable quartic term, with no upper limit on positive c. Below the negative boundary the energy is unbounded below; at that boundary the quadratic term also requires checking. The tool reports boundedness and continuously degenerate solutions separately rather than treating the lowest plotted point as a stable phase. At positive c=2√(b1b2), particular quadratic coefficients can also yield an ellipse of minima.

sections.title: coexisting solutions come from simultaneous equations
sections.text: to non-zero Q₁, Q₂ Let x=Q₁², y=Q₂². Solving the linear equation also requires x,y>0 and checks the Hessian; two non-zero components do not automatically mean stable coexistence.

sections.title: compares all stable candidates
sections.text: The origin, single-mode solutions, and mixed solutions are all included in the comparison. A positive c tends to penalize the simultaneous occurrence of two modes; the minimum on the free energy surface describes the model equilibrium and does not give the true domain wall or transition rate.

lessons.title: From exchange energy to ferromagnetic spin wave
lessons.summary: turns the cost of small spin deviations into propagable collective excitations.

sections.title: defines symbols and physical units
sections.text: The ferromagnetic chain uses an exchange Hamiltonian with an overall minus sign and J>0; Δ≥1 is easy-axis XXZ exchange anisotropy. h is a Zeeman energy in meV that already includes gμB, not a magnetic field in Tesla.

sections.title: linearization retains only small movements
sections.text: unfolds around a collinear reference state along +z, neglecting higher-order interactions between excitations. S is the spin quantum number; the animated small-angle amplitudes are for demonstration purposes only and do not represent thermal occupation at a given temperature.

sections.title: Gapless and gapped cases follow from the same formula
sections.text: When Δ=1, h=0, q=0 uniformly rotates without energy penalty. Easy-axis anisotropy or a positive field along the reference magnetic moment can open the energy gap.

sections.title: wavevector See with phase
sections.text: The axis q of the graph on this site represents qa/π; ferromagnetic The first Brillouin zone is [−1,1]. Move wavevector to observe the phase difference between adjacent spins, and then use the time/phase cursor to observe the precession.

lessons.title: Two antiferromagnetic polarizations and field splitting
lessons.summary: The coupling of two opposing sublattices makes the motion different from that of two independent ferromagnetic chains.

sections.title: Magnetic periodicity changes the Brillouin zone
sections.text: Néel Magnetism of the reference state primitive cell contains two sublattices. Based on the nearest neighbor distance a, the reduced area is qa/π∈[−1/2,1/2]; it cannot be directly regarded as the complete interval of the ferromagnetic chain.

sections.title: Two sublattices require a coupled diagonalization
sections.text: unfolds in two sublattice localized quantization axes, with positive and negative frequencies and conjugate amplitudes appearing in pairs. The physically positive branch comes from transformations that preserve Bose commutation relations .

sections.title: Longitudinal field separates two polarizations
sections.text: The two modes about a stable Néel background shift by ±h. Reassess the reference state when a signed branch reaches zero.

sections.title: model spectrum is separated from the real material
sections.text: First study the mechanism in chains with a small number of sublattices, then explore the background of antiferromagnetic materials such as MnF₂. The teaching chain's parameters, dimensionality, and spectrum are not a quantitative fit to MnF₂. Linear spin-wave theory also does not fully describe one-dimensional quantum chains at small S.

lessons.title: Before drawing the spectrum, check the reference state first
lessons.summary: soft mode , signed energy and unstable background require different interpretations.

sections.title: Isotropic limit provides benchmark
sections.text: At Δ=1 and h=0, the long-wavelength ferromagnetic excitation energy vanishes as q², whereas the antiferromagnetic linear-spin-wave energy vanishes as |q|. These limits independently check the discrete formulas and coordinate conventions.

sections.title: static phase change threshold should also be checked
sections.text: A longitudinal field in an easy-axis antiferromagnet can cause spin reorientation or canting. The site displays both the classical ground-state range and the reference small-oscillation spectrum; outside that range, it disables precession animations that would incorrectly treat the original background as stable.

sections.title: The phase cursor at zero frequency is not a real finite period
sections.text: A uniform zero-energy mode has no finite oscillation period. Mode vectors may become singular in a low-energy limit; the program must explain this instead of producing infinite amplitudes or a false period.

sections.title: from spin group to observable excitation
sections.text: Compares models that preserve and destroy continuous spin rotation, explaining changes in the energy gap. The full neutron scattering intensity also requires magnetic shape factors, geometry and correlation functions, and this first edition shows dispersion and linear modes.

lessons.title: Thermal expansion results from the competition of free energy of different volumes
lessons.summary: Cv for a fixed volume and equilibrium volume as a function of temperature are two different issues.

sections.title: First prepare a set of compatible data
sections.text: Every volume requires static energy and vibrational free energy with the same cell normalization, atom count, temperature grid and energy units. Each volume must have its own corresponding phonon calculation; one DOS cannot simply be assigned repeatedly to different volumes.

sections.title: Add static and vibration contributions
sections.text: phonon Free energy includes zero point energy and temperature terms, but does not include static electron ground state energy. The external pressure enters the objective function through pV.

sections.title: Temperature changes equilibrium position
sections.text: phonon The volume dependence of the free energy changes the total free energy minimum as the temperature changes. Adjust the temperature cursor and observe the movement of the scatter points, fitted curve, and V_{eq}.

sections.title: Current calculation method and material meaning
sections.text: This experiment uses an explicitly given local low-order polynomial fit and does not pretend to be a general-purpose equation-of-state solver. A built-in volume-dependent Einstein model is used to verify the mechanism; quantitative material results require the user to import and check volume versus temperature convergence.

lessons.title: Obtain thermal expansion and C_p from equilibrium free energy
lessons.summary: Specify fixed variables before deriving derivatives and retain unit conversion.

sections.title: volume expansion coefficient
sections.text: α_V is the derivative of equilibrium volume with respect to temperature divided by volume. Only with isotropic expansion, the linear expansion coefficient is equal to α_V/3; a volume path cannot automatically give a general anisotropic expansion tensor.

sections.title: constant pressure heat capacity comes from minimized G
sections.text: First minimize the volume for each temperature, and then find the second-order temperature derivative with respect to G(T,p). The Cv of a fixed volume comes from the derivative of F(T,V) under the same volume, and the two cannot exchange labels.

sections.title: Volume curvature determines the bulk modulus
sections.text: Positive volume curvature at the equilibrium point gives the isothermal bulk modulus. If the fitting minimum is at the input volume boundary, reliable curvature and equilibrium volume cannot be calculated solely based on boundary extension.

sections.title: Endpoints and noise of numerical differentiation
sections.text: Only interior temperatures have data on both sides. Derived α_V/C_p are not reported at the first and last temperatures. Second derivatives amplify fit noise, so compare temperature steps and volume windows.

lessons.title: How to judge whether a thermal expansion curve is credible?
lessons.summary: Checks the effective minimum, fit residuals, volume window and data source.

sections.title: Sample volumes covering at least the neighborhood of the minimum
sections.text: requires five or more different volumes and verifies that the temperature grid is consistent. The lowest point of each temperature should be covered by the sample; when a boundary occurs, the volume range is expanded and the input data is recalculated.

sections.title: Fitting goodness is not equal to physical convergence
sections.text: Small residuals only indicate that the function is close to the current sample. It is necessary to add volume points, change the fitting window and order, and check the changes in equilibrium volume and bulk modulus. phonon q Grid convergence should be verified separately during the data production phase.

sections.title: Near a phase transition, the model needs extra care
sections.text: The free energies of different structural branches should be established separately before comparison. In soft mode or significantly anharmonic regions, a single stable harmonic reference state of quasiharmonic approximation may fail; this tool does not generate anharmonic force constants or thermal conductivities.

sections.title: Save the calculation process as a research record
sections.text: Exports the original energy, units, temperature grid, pressure, fitting settings, residuals and invalid point causes of each volume. Keeping old records during recalculation can explain why the curve changed.

exercises.title: periodic boundaries and reference unit cells
exercises.prompt: The one-dimensional length is 4 Å, with parent fractional coordinate 0.98 and distorted coordinate 0.02; there is no strain.

steps.prompt: What is the fractional-coordinate difference before periodic-image correction?
steps.hint: first calculates 0.02−0.98.
steps.explanation: The original difference is −0.96, and periodic mirroring has not been selected.

steps.prompt: What is the fractional-coordinate difference after selecting the nearest periodic image?
steps.hint: adds an integer shift to the original difference.

steps.prompt: What is the actual shortest displacement?
steps.hint: times the lattice length 4 Å.

steps.prompt: Can non-orthogonal three-dimensional unit cells always be folded back component by component?
choices: No, Cartesian length should be compared
steps.hint: There are cross-metric terms between lattice vectors.
steps.explanation: The true Cartesian norm must be minimized in the tilted unit cell.

exercises.title: Orthogonal projection and residual
exercises.prompt: takes b₁=(1,1)/√2, b₂=(1,−1)/√2, and u=(√2,0) in the two-dimensional displacement subspace.

steps.prompt: What is the inner product of b₁ and b₂?
steps.hint: expands the product of two components.

steps.prompt: Q₁=b₁·u equal to?
steps.hint: Only the first component of u is nonzero.

steps.prompt: Q₂ equal to?
steps.hint: computes the product of the first component of b₂ and √2.
steps.explanation: Q₂=1, so both modes jointly reconstruct u.

steps.prompt: only retains b₁, what is the residual norm?
steps.hint: The missing component is Q₂b₂, with normalized b₂.

exercises.title: How do competition parameters change the balance amplitude?
exercises.prompt: Take a₁=a₂=−1, b₁=b₂=1, c=1 and find the symmetric mixed solution.

steps.prompt: Let x=Q₁², y=Q₂², what is the first equation?
steps.hint: Substitute the parameters into 2b₁x+cy=−a₁.

steps.prompt: What is the symmetric solution x=y?
steps.hint: Substitute y=x into the first formula.

steps.prompt: What is the free energy of the mixed solution?
steps.hint: into −x−y+x²+y²+xy.

steps.prompt: The lowest single mode is −1/4, which one is lower?
steps.hint: compares two negative numbers.
steps.explanation: −1/3<−1/4, and the Hessian of the mixed solution is positive, this set of parameters coexists stably.

exercises.title: hand-calculated energy gap and bandwidth of ferromagnetic chain
exercises.prompt: takes J=1 meV, S=1, Δ=1.2, h=0.1 meV.

steps.prompt: What is the cosine at q=0?
steps.explanation: The cosine of the uniform mode is 1.

steps.prompt: What is the energy at q=0?
What is the energy at qa=π?
steps.hint: cos π=−1。

steps.prompt: What is the difference between the two?
steps.hint: Subtract the zone center energy from the zone boundary energy.

exercises.title: antiferromagnetic branched magnetic field splitting
exercises.prompt: takes J=S=1, Δ=1.25, q=0, h=0.2 meV.

steps.prompt: What is the number in the root of zero field?
steps.hint: calculates Δ²−1.

steps.prompt: What is the zero field energy ε₀?
steps.hint: Multiply the square-root result by 2JS.

steps.prompt: Which group of two energies are they?
steps.hint: subtract and add h respectively.

steps.prompt: What is the size of the magnetic field split?
steps.hint: The difference between the two is equal to 2h.

exercises.title: Long Wave Limit and Goldstone Mode
exercises.prompt: Let Δ=1, h=0, compare the ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic models under small qa.

steps.prompt: What is the lowest order term of 1−cos(qa) in the ferromagnetic formula?
steps.hint: Use the Taylor expansion of cosines.

steps.prompt: What is the lowest order form of ferromagnetic ε?
steps.hint: Multiply the previous equation by 2JS.
steps.explanation: ferromagnetic long wave dispersion is quadratic type.

steps.prompt: antiferromagnetic √(1−cos²qa) equals?
steps.hint: Use trigonometric identities and preserve absolute values.

steps.prompt: antiferromagnetic What is the lowest order form of long wave ε?
choices: Zero, the entire interval is zero
steps.hint: Small angle sin x≈x.
steps.explanation: The antiferromagnetic long-wavelength branch of the linear spin wave is linear; the zero point is only at the corresponding wavevector .

exercises.title: Why does pressure tend to decrease in volume?
exercises.prompt: Comparing two points at the same temperature: V₁=40 Å³ and V₂=42 Å³, the total free energy at zero pressure is the same and the external pressure is positive.

steps.prompt: Which one needs to be included?
steps.hint: Using Gibbs free energy at fixed pressure.
steps.explanation: The function to be minimized of G contains +pV.

steps.prompt: Which one has a greater pV under positive pressure?
steps.hint: The pressure is the same and the volume is greater, the product is greater.
steps.explanation: The pV of V₂=42 Å³ is larger.

steps.prompt: Of these two candidates with originally identical free energies, which one is more advantageous?
choices: Cannot be compared based on any criteria
steps.hint: Compare the total amount after adding pV.
steps.explanation: Positive pressure makes the total free energy of V₁ lower.

steps.prompt: Can V(T) be determined with only a fixed-volume DOS?
choices: No, volume dependent data is required
steps.hint: Minimization requires comparison between different volumes.
steps.explanation: Equilibrium volume cannot be determined without volume-dependent E(V) and F_{vib}(T,V).

exercises.title: Finding response from analytical curve
exercises.prompt: Let V(T)=V₀(1+aT), G(T)=G₀−bT²/2, a,b>0, use consistent units.

steps.prompt: What is dV/dT?
steps.hint: Derive the linear temperature term.

steps.prompt: What is α_V?
steps.hint: Divide the derivative by the current volume.

steps.prompt: What is d²G/dT²?
steps.hint: Find the derivative of −bT²/2 twice consecutively.

steps.prompt: What is C_p?
steps.hint: C_p=−TG″。

exercises.title: Identifying volumetric extrapolation and false convergence
exercises.prompt: In the input range of 36–44 Å³, the fitting free energy still continues to decrease as the volume increases.

steps.prompt: Is there a bracketed interior minimum within the sampled interval?
steps.hint: The descending function does not have an internal minimum.
steps.explanation: does not cover the minimum, 44 Å³ is only the sampling boundary.

steps.prompt: What is the appropriate next step?
choices: directly extrapolates ten times the volume
calls the boundary an equilibrium state
Expand the volume range and make additional calculations
steps.hint: requires new physics input, not just changing the plot axes.
steps.explanation: should be supplemented by covering the minimum near volume point calculated with phonon .

steps.prompt: Can small fitting residuals prove q grid convergence?
steps.hint: fitting error and the phonon sampling error come from different steps.
steps.explanation: residuals only evaluate the current data fit and do not validate the original phonon grid.

steps.prompt: temperature endpoint lacks data on both sides, how does this tool handle C_p?
choices: Do not report and explain the reason
steps.hint: Don't disguise missing derivatives as physical results.
steps.explanation: Endpoint derived quantity is empty, more temperature data support is required.

cases.title: Express polar distortions in mode coordinates
cases.summary: Start from an ideal parent cell and relative Ti/O displacements, reconstruct modes, then study competition using two-order-parameter free energy.
cases.assumption: structure and pattern are original ideal teaching models; Landau coefficients are not automatically fitted by the structure.

cases.title: Compatible supercells and antiphase oxygen-octahedron rotations
cases.summary: Observe linear displacements of alternating rotations in 2×2×2 supercell , projecting and reconstructing the same distortion.
cases.assumption: Small displacement mode description; does not interpret arbitrary amplitudes as strictly rigid octahedrons or true temperature phase diagrams.

cases.title: From opposite moments to paired magnetic excitations
cases.summary: Compare ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic exchange, observing anisotropy, external fields and sublattice precession.
cases.assumption: one-dimensional linear spin wave teaching model; MnF₂ is only used as an existing three-dimensional material background and does not use chain parameters to pretend to be quantitative spectra.

cases.title: From vibration free energy to thermal expansion
cases.summary: Compare the volume dependence of temperature, pressure and frequency, import your own multi-volume data and save research records.
cases.assumption: The built-in Einstein frequencies, static energies, and parameters are original teaching constructions, not first-principles data for a material.
